parsed.explanation: The combined regime pairs a documented hostile national layer with a comparatively restrained division. Universal traveller-facing exposure exists at entry: the February 2025 cable directs refusal where documents cast doubt on sex, permits fraud-referral toward lifetime ineligibility, and has already triggered advisories from eight-plus governments; passport-marker litigation is unresolved. Nationally, facility bans operate in roughly 20 states with criminal trespass in four and one documented arrest, plus documented conversion-therapy-style custody and immigration-detention abuse. This division itself sits in the July 2026 low-risk group, retains employment/public-accommodation protections, and its governor vetoed bathroom bills; but it lacks state hate-crime cover, retains the trans-panic defence, restricts trans minors, and Pride organising has collapsed. No local adult-specific arrest is documented, though that silence is not proof of safety.

entry_documents.exposure: National cable instructs officers to refuse cases where documents or records cast reasonable doubt on an applicant's sex, with fraud/lifetime-ineligibility referral considered for suspected misrepresentation; passport X-markers barred; travellers report confiscated or blocked passports; multiple governments issued travel advisories. Litigation unresolved.
entry_documents.protection: Fraud finding requires all four statutory elements, is never automatic, and has limited waivers; existing X-marker passports remain valid until expiry; a legal-aid FAQ tracks the rules.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry refusal interacts with onward state-level facility and document rules, compounding exposure across the visit.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National custody documented: conversion-therapy-style corrections policies (hair cutting, hormone removal) from 2026, immigration-detention forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and sexual abuse of trans men; a trans woman held 24 hours in a men's ward after a bathroom arrest in another state. Gay/trans-panic defence remains available in this division.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No trans-specific arrest or detention documented in this division; national hate-crime statute covers gender identity since 2009; courts have enjoined several orders.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A visitor entering immigration custody or prison would fall under the national custody regime; division protections do not reach federal facilities.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Nationally, facility bans cover all government buildings in 10 units, schools plus some government buildings in 9 more, schools-only in 3; 6 units extend bans to private settings; 4 states make it a criminal offence; one documented arrest under such a law. Map notes other laws may further restrict access.
federal_state_facilities.protection: This division's governor vetoed bathroom and pronoun bills in June 2023; it sits in the low-risk group; 29 states plus capital district have no mapped ban. Whether this division carries an unmapped ban is not documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Visitors moving between states carry the strictest encountered rule; federal funding conditions can induce local adoption.

care_services.exposure: This division bars sex-reassignment surgery on trans children (2022) and restricts trans girls from female sports; nationally an October 2025 rule would bar public-insurance reimbursement for under-18 care and January 2025 orders call minor care 'mutilation'. A 1982 Medicaid surgery exclusion remains on the books with unresolved litigation.
care_services.protection: June 2023 executive order gives state employees over 21 full gender-affirming Medicaid/insurance coverage; conversion therapy defunded by 2023 order; adult visitor care access is not documented as restricted here.
care_services.interaction: A travelling family with a trans minor faces the division's youth restrictions plus national political framing; an adult alone faces little documented care barrier.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National executive orders define sex binary at conception, ban gender-ideology funding and name/pronoun use, direct law enforcement to investigate schools promoting 'gender ideology', and a May 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritises neutralising groups 'radically pro-transgender'; a December 2025 reward memo references 'radical gender ideology' among extremist animating viewpoints. 66% of the public backs birth-sex document listing.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: The reward memo never uses the phrase as a criterion; the strategy states counterterrorism powers will not target mere disagreement; several orders blocked or enjoined; this division's executive has actively vetoed anti-trans bills.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: National framing raises the social cost of being outed even where division law is restrained, and influences police discretion during stops.

minors_guardians.exposure: Division bans trans children from female sports and bars childhood transition surgery; Department of Education hotline invites reporting of 'gender ideology' in schools; nationally an order directs criminal prosecution of teachers facilitating a trans minor's social transition and an order labels minor care 'mutilation'. Judges judged these youth policies unlikely to extend to adults, criteria unspecified.
minors_guardians.protection: Assessment groups this division as low-risk and says youth policies are unlikely to extend to adults; courts narrowly limited family-court intervention; a trans-visibility visit without school enrolment largely avoids the youth regime.
minors_guardians.interaction: A parent travelling with a trans minor could attract scrutiny under youth framing even though the criminal provisions target in-state schools and teachers, not visitors.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-directed violence incident is documented in this division, but that silence is not evidence of safety; the trans-panic defence remains available, state hate-crime law omits gender identity, Pride events in the second-largest city were cancelled in January 2026 and the organising body dissolved citing an environment making queer events nearly impossible.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; municipal ordinances in nine cities ban gender-identity discrimination in public accommodations; national statistics show bias incidents are recorded and reported.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Absence of state bias coverage weakens recourse if an assault occurs, while the national statute still supplies a charging option.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Several national orders are enjoined but litigation is unresolved; the passport suit proceeds yet the restriction operates; the 1982 Medicaid exclusion's interaction with later orders is unresolved; Low-Risk criteria unspecified; municipal ordinances carry broad exemptions; no documented local remedy process for trans visitors.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Functioning courts have blocked or enjoined multiple orders, permitted birth-certificate marker change without surgery (August 2024), and award relief; a legal-aid FAQ and civil-liberties litigation provide real, if slow, recourse.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies operate mainly for residents litigating; a short-term visitor often departs before any remedy matures.

anchor_checks.comparison: Higher than 0.35-A: Vellandra's register excludes transgender visitors outright with near-zero remedy and universal airline verification. Here entry refusal is discretionary, tied to documented doubt about sex, and retains waiver and judicial-review routes; no registration or exclusion regime reaches every crossing.

Somewhat higher than 0.55-B: Kestrel Isles' secondary screening with slow, rarely revised refusal appeals resembles the sex-doubt refusal cable. But this jurisdiction adds documented employment and accommodation protections, an executive that vetoes anti-trans bills, and courts that grant relief, lowering everyday severity beyond border friction.

Lower than 0.75-C: Meridia's border officers are trained and respectful with compensation for unlawful holding. Here officers are affirmatively instructed to doubt sex on document discrepancy, other governments have issued advisories, the hostile national custody and facilities regimes apply, and remedies are unresolved rather than reliably protective.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller meets one system: a national layer that is genuinely traveller-facing (sex-doubt refusal at entry with fraud-referral exposure, X-marker elimination, advisory-issuing governments, custody abuse if detained, facility bans and a criminal trespass arrest elsewhere) layered on a division that restrains adult-targeting. The division's documented positives — vetoed bathroom bills, low-risk classification, employment and accommodation ordinances, functioning courts that have won injunctions and marker changes — meaningfully soften everyday exposure, while its gaps (no state hate-crime cover, trans-panic defence, youth restrictions, collapsed Pride infrastructure) and the unresolved national litigation keep it below the trained-border, working-remedy tier. For an adult alone: entry friction plus street-level friction, no credible imprisonment. With a trans minor: youth-targeting rules and national framing add a further step down.
